chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Teddy Weatherford and Glover Compton
summary: Caldwell doubts Earl Hines copied Teddy Weatherford; Glover Compton was more an entertainer at the piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Teddy Weatherford, sure, I knew Teddy well.
Well, I mean they have that thing. Some of these people say that they think Earl copied from Teddy.
That's what a lot of them say.
When you hear the records that
Teddy, that he made in Paris in 1935-36, well, there's nothing like Earl (unintelligible), a very much simpler style.
But not as good as Fats.
Right. No, I don't think that Earl copied after him, between you and I.
No. And what about that other one, Glover --
Glover Compton? Well, Glover more -- is more of a fellow to entertain on the piano.
That's what type he was. Glover (unintelligible) -- used to go and see Glover. You know, he remind you Glover, a lot of Jelly Roll --
